title: Crystal Johnson — City of Promise
body: ← Back to team Crystal Johnson Community School Director Phone 434.295.9525 Email Crystal Bio About Crystal. Crystal Johnson is a Charlottesville native who lives in the City of Promise footprint with her family. Crystal is a dedicated Community School Director with a passion for community engagement. In her role, Crystal oversees a variety of initiatives aimed at enhancing the educational experience for students and providing essential resources for families. Crystal is committed to creating a supportive and inclusive environment that bridges community and schools. Outside of her professional life, Crystal is passionate about theater, and making sure everyone has access to come alive on stage. Crystal believes in the power of education to transform lives and is dedicated to making a positive difference in her community. My mission is to strengthen the bond between community, school, and families, ensuring every child feels supported, nurtured, and inspired to learn. — Crystal Johnson

title: Dawn Lawson — City of Promise
body: ← Back to team Dawn Lawson Family Empowerment Coach Phone 434.989.2593 Email Dawn Bio About Dawn. A native of Charlottesville, Dawn Lawson attended Virginia Wesleyan College where she was scholarship chairman for Phi Sigma Sigma. Dawn received her master s degree in Human Service/Marriage and Family Counseling from Liberty University. Her community service has included participation in Make a Difference Day and fundraisers for the National Kidney Foundation at VWC, as well as volunteering with Love Inc. and Covenant Church. Her work experience includes case management, substance abuse counseling, working with at-risk children in a school setting, and community-based services that included teaching her clients skills to achieve their goals, and working with families in the foster care system. Dawn would love to become a foster parent. She loves sports and animals. I want to encourage, motivate, and help others recognize their strengths so they can reach their personal goals. In return, they can take their skills to empower and uplift others. — Dawn Lawson

title: Jamaala Hamilton — City of Promise
body: ← Back to team Jamaala Hamilton Community School Coordinator Phone 434.282.3572 Email Jamaala Bio About Jamaala. Originally from Orange County, Jamaala Hamilton moved to Charlottesville as a teenager and graduated from Charlottesville High School. She began her career in community work through property management, with roles at Greenstone on 5th, Kindlewood, and Carlton View Apartments. While working in the rental office, she realized that her impact could be far greater outside the confines of a desk, in the community. Her passion for helping others led her to City of Promise, which she describes as the missing link for so many individuals and families she connects with daily.

title: Jamar Henderson — City of Promise
body: ← Back to team Jamar Henderson Community School Coordinator Phone 434.295.9525 Email Jamar Bio About Jamar. Jamar Henderson was raised in Charlottesville, graduating in 2008 as a CHS Black Knight! He brings to City of Promise extensive experience as a youth counselor, mentor, and case manager, serving most recently at the Chesterfield County Juvenile Detention Center and People Places in Charlottesville. He previously worked at the Albemarle County Regional Jail as a corrections officer, and has extensive experience in trauma-informed practices, crisis intervention, and mental health support. In addition to pathway coaching, Jamar works with middle schoolers involved in the Starr Hill Pathways program of the UVA Equity Center.

title: Jermaine Dias — City of Promise
body: ← Back to team Jermaine Dias Assistant Director Phone 551.404.5832 Email Jermaine Bio About Jermaine. Jermaine Dias has more than a decade of experience working with youth in public education. A native of Hackensack, New Jersey, Jermaine is a 2007 graduate of the University of Virginia and an alumnus of the Cavalier football team. He has spent the majority of his career serving as both a mental health specialist and high school football coach throughout the Charlottesville-Albemarle area. Jermaine and his wife Tamara have been married since 2017, and they love to cheer on their National Champion Hoos! I know what it is like to overcome being labeled troublemaker, only to change my behavior and be labeled as the invisible C student. I want students to know that they matter, and that there is someone advocating for them. — Jermaine Dias

title: Melissa Steppe — City of Promise
body: ← Back to team Melissa Steppe Director of Parent Engagement & Advocacy Phone 434.421.5635 Email Melissa Bio About Melissa. Melissa Steppe-Mattox, a proud native of Charlottesville, Virginia, is a dedicated advocate for youth empowerment and education. She earned her degree in social work from George Mason University and is currently advancing her expertise by pursuing a master s degree in the same field. After graduating in 2010, Melissa returned to Charlottesville and founded her youth consulting business, Steppe into Change, LLC. For over 10 years, she provided mentoring services to local youth through the Charlottesville-Albemarle County Department of Social Services. During this time, she also joined the City of Promise team as a pathway coach for 5th- to 8th-grade students. Melissa treasures her time with her family, especially cheering on her children in their various extra-curricular activities. Her enthusiasm for rejoining the City of Promise team reflects her deep commitment to enriching and supporting the community she loves.

title: Price Thomas — City of Promise
body: ← Back to team Price A. Thomas Executive Director Phone 434.228.5153 Email Price Bio About Price. Price was named Executive Director in May 2023. Born and raised in Charlottesville, Price Thomas brings extensive experience as a communications expert and campaign strategist in addition to his deep knowledge of the Charlottesville community. His nonprofit leadership experience with both the Montpelier Foundation and United Way combined with his dedication to young people, made him the ideal choice to follow in the impactful footsteps of departing Executive Director, Mary Coleman. Price noted, I m humbled and thrilled to have the opportunity to build on the strong existing foundation at City of Promise and continue the work that Mary and the staff are doing. I owe a debt of gratitude to the leadership of the United Way and I m looking forward to applying what I ve learned to growing the scope and impact of City of Promise. I was raised here, I m raising my kids here, and I m excited for the opportunity to have a positive impact on the place I call home. I want to create opportunities and access for children and parents so that no one has their dreams deferred. — Price Thomas

title: City of Promise — Community Schools
body: Program 01 · Community Schools 75% fewer missed days. Community School Coordinators embedded inside seven Charlottesville school sites — coaching kids, brokering resources for families, and closing the literacy gap one classroom at a time. 01 In their own words "A real, specific story about one kid, one walk to school, one parent meeting that changed something." — Coordinator name, Community School Coordinator 02 Our Model Coordinators embedded inside seven schools. Community Schools is built on the national Community Schools framework and Virginia Literacy Partnerships, adapted for Charlottesville's geography. A full-time Community School Coordinator (CSC) is placed inside each of seven school sites: ELC, Trailblazer, Tall Oaks, Summit, CMS, Lugo-McGinness, and CHS. Community Schools framework Virginia Literacy Partnerships The coordinator is the connective tissue — not the executor of every program component, but the person who knows the family, refers students into VLP tutoring, manages the on-site food pantry, coordinates the Walking Bus volunteers, and stays through the handoff to other CoP programs and Charlottesville's wider safety net. Note: this work was previously called "Pathway Coaching." The model and coordinators are the same; the name is updated. 03 Inside the Program 01 The Coordinator Role Coach, resource broker, and family liaison — the hub that connects the other mechanisms to the family. The coordinator knows the kid, knows the parent, and is the same person from week to week. 02 After-School Tutoring Four days a week, K–12. The coordinator refers students in based on what they see in the classroom and at home; VLP-certified tutors deliver the instruction. 03 On-Site Food Pantries Backpack model. The coordinator manages on-site distribution; food is sourced and stocked by an external Charlottesville partner organization. (partner to confirm) 04 The Walking Bus Trailblazer-specific. 25–30 kids walked to school every day by a rotating team of volunteers from the Nurturing Neighborhood pilot. The coordinator coordinates; volunteers walk. 04 By the Numbers The receipts. 7 school sites 75% drop in average absences (Spring → Fall 2025) 40+ added instructional hours per student 49pp Charlottesville's literacy pass-rate gap, the highest in Virginia 05 The Team Behind It Director + seven coordinators. title: City of Promise — Dreambuilders
body: Program 02 · Dreambuilders Two years. One family. A two-year wraparound for working Charlottesville families: weekly classes, family learning time, embedded coaching, and up to $7,000 in stipends toward goals families set for themselves. In their own words "This program has helped me gain tools to be independent and self-disciplined." — Dreambuilders participant, Class of 2025 Our Model A two-year wraparound, built on evidence. Dreambuilders is built on the National Center for Families Learning (NCFL) family literacy model. Cohorts of working Charlottesville parents commit to a two-year program — a full school year of weekly classes followed by a lighter year of continued support — anchored on three touchpoints: Parent Time, P.A.C.T. Time, and 1:1 coaching with a Family Empowerment Coach. NCFL family literacy model Cohort-based Two-year commitment Each family receives a $5,000 stipend in year one and $2,000 in year two — $7,000 across the program — paired with goals each family sets for themselves. The coach is in the room when those goals are made. Structured as agency, not charity. Inside the Program 01 Parent Time Weekly classes for parents only — parenting practices, financial literacy, working with CCS, advocacy skills, peer connection. Runs the full school year (36–38 weeks). Childcare provided on-site so attendance doesn't depend on it. 02 P.A.C.T. Time (Parents and Children Together) Guided parent-and-child learning time. Parents learn to be the educator, not just the audience. Weekly cadence, structured around shared activities, with a coach in the room. 03 Family Empowerment Coaches 1:1 coaching across the full two years. Same coach the whole way through — continuity is the point. The coach helps the family weigh the goals they set for themselves and signs off on stipend decisions alongside them. 04 Stipend Support $5,000 in year one and $2,000 in year two — $7,000 across the program. Families set the goals; the stipend covers what comes up: car repairs to keep a job, housing deposits, certification courses, deferred medical co-pays. By the Numbers What two years can do. 78% of FY25 participants increased self-sufficiency & completed goals 2 yr wraparound commitment per family $7K stipend support across the program 26 adults + youth reached through the FY25 cohort The Team Behind It Director + Family Empowerment Coaches. title: City of Promise — Family Engagement & Advocacy
body: Program 03 · Family Engagement & Advocacy The phone tree is a person. Brokerage with continuity. The same coach goes to the IEP meeting, makes the housing call, and stays through the handoff to Charlottesville's wider safety net — no application, no cohort, ongoing intake. In their own words "A specific moment a coach showed up — the morning after the eviction notice, the call that got the housing application unstuck, the IEP meeting where the parent didn't have to walk in alone." — Parent name, F&E participant Our Model Brokerage with continuity — the same coach across the full handoff. Family Engagement & Advocacy is the parent-facing arm of City of Promise's dual-generation model: parenting practices coaching, school advocacy, and connection to the wider Charlottesville safety net. No application required. No cohort. Ongoing intake. Resource brokers No application required Ongoing intake The mechanism is brokerage with continuity: the coach who knows the family is the same person who knows which Charlottesville organization has the right service, and stays alongside the family through the handoff so it doesn't drop. F&E is often the first touchpoint that brings a family deeper into Community Schools or Dreambuilders. Inside the Program 01 Parenting Practices Coaching 1:1 coaching on the day-to-day craft — discipline, school engagement, routines, sibling dynamics. Frame: parenting as a set of practices, not a personality trait. 02 School Advocacy Going to the IEP meeting with the parent, calling the principal, working through transfers and discipline issues. CoP shows up for the family, not for the institution. 03 Community Resource Connection Brokerage into housing, childcare, health, food, transportation, legal, and employment services. The differentiator vs. a referral: the coach stays with the family through the handoff. The Constellation of Care The map of the orgs we broker into. Housing, childcare, health, food, transportation, legal, employment. F&E coaches don't run those services — Charlottesville's existing organizations do. F&E's job is to know which organization fits which family, and to stay with the family until the handoff sticks. View the Constellation of Care → By the Numbers What brokerage looks like. title: Our Approach — City of Promise
body: On this page The Problem Constellation of Care Dual-Generation Theory of Change By the Numbers Our Approach Education is a social issue. A child's learning starts outside the classroom, in the household and the neighborhood that shape the school day before the bell rings. 01 The Problem why we exist In Charlottesville, the literacy gap between Black and White students is 49 percentage points. It's the highest in Virginia. VDOE Standards of Learning, 2024 The kids we work with come to class carrying chronic absenteeism, household instability, and a life that school alone can't fix. 3rd–8th Grade Reading SOL · Pass Rate by Race The Charlottesville reading gap, in context. 82% White 33% Black Cville 76% White 52% Black VA Avg 72% White 61% Black Best VA Div The gap isn't "bad in Charlottesville." It's the worst. The failure isn't in the teachers, the curriculum, or the funding. It's in the load a child carries into the classroom from outside of it. SRC: VDOE SOL 2024 $18.5K Cost per pupil, per year CCS spends more per child than the state average. Outcomes haven't followed. 1 in 3 Chronically absent Missing ≥10% of school days, the leading indicator for every downstream gap. 49 pp Literacy gap, highest in VA Black vs White reading-SOL pass rates, 3rd–8th grade. Detail above. 02 The Constellation of Care how it fits together A child's ability to learn is predicated on stability across all dimensions. Click on an area to learn more. See the programs → 03 Dual-Generation Model who we reach Most programs pick a lane. We do both, in the same household, at the same time. Reach the kid, or reach the parent. Most organizations can only afford to choose one. The dual-generation model is the bet that you have to do both, together, or the gains don't compound. Child-side What we do for the kid Embedded Pathway Coach at their school On-site tutoring during the school day Walking Bus to and from class Food pantry access when the household needs it Parent-side What we do for the parent Parent Time, the weekly cohort P.A.C.T. Time, structured parent-child engagement Up to $7K micro-financing, matched to family goals School navigation and advocacy 04 Theory of Change the argument You can't fix a child's outcomes without changing the household around them. Three assumptions. Take any one away and the model collapses. Assumption 1 Proximity matters Services inside the school the child already attends. Not a referral across town. Assumption 2 Parents first A parent who's thriving is the single biggest predictor of a child who's thriving. Assumption 3 Relationship, not triage A coach who knows the family's name, and has been there for two years, can do what a case manager can't. 05 By the Numbers the proof Sixteen years in. Here's what the model produces. 327 kids in our programs FY25 94% avg. attendance vs 78% baseline 41 Dreambuilders grads since 2022 7 school sites Charlottesville Next Now see it in practice. The three programs on What We Do put this argument into practice. What We Do → Donate

title: Volunteer — City of Promise
body: On this page Nurturing Neighborhood Mentoring & Transportation Reading Tutoring How to sign up Get Involved — Volunteer We can't make change alone. Kids spend about 80% of their waking hours out of school. That time is either a tailwind or a headwind. CoP volunteers are how it becomes a tailwind. We run three volunteer roles, each one a relationship with a kid or family in Westhaven or 10th and Page that runs at least a full school semester, often longer. 01 The Work Repeat contact, same families. Every role pairs you with a small group of kids or families and asks you to stay with them through a full school semester at minimum . Most volunteers stay through the year. CoP does not run event-day shifts, one-off drives, or surge volunteering. The work is repeat contact with the same families on a regular schedule, because that is what changes a child's trajectory. Before you scroll Background check is universal across every role. CoP runs and pays for it. All roles are place-based in Charlottesville. Westhaven, 10th and Page, and seven CCS partner schools, including Trailblazer, Summit, and Tall Oaks. Reading Tutoring requires VA Literacy Partnerships certification. Online plus practicum, roughly 12 hours over 4 weeks. Paid for by CoP. Plan to commit through at least one school semester. Most volunteers stay a full year. 02·a Nurturing Neighborhood When parents thrive, children thrive. What it is Nurturing Neighborhood is a faith-partner pilot CoP runs with the Thomas Jefferson Memorial Church Unitarian Universalist congregation and City Church . A pod of 4–5 volunteers is matched to one family in Westhaven or 10th and Page and stays with that family over months and years. What you'd do Pods address the everyday non-monetary barriers a family faces: rides to appointments, after-school pickup, moving help, an extra adult at a school meeting. CoP staff coordinate scheduling and check-ins, and brief each pod before placement. 4–5 volunteers per pod Multi-yr horizon per family 2 active families Partner Pilot UU + City Church Westhaven 10th and Page Sign up for Nurturing Neighborhood → 02·b Mentoring & Transportation Rides plus mentorship for CCS extracurriculars. What it is CoP volunteers drive Charlottesville City Schools students to and from sports practices, music lessons, and other extracurriculars they would otherwise miss for lack of transportation. The mentorship happens in the car, on repeated trips with the same kid. What you'd do Two to four trips per week during the season, typically afternoons and early evenings. CoP matches volunteers to students based on geography, schedule, and the kid's activity. 2–4 trips per week 1:1 volunteer to student 3 match windows per year CCS partner schools Mentoring Transportation Sports + Music Seasonal Matching Sign up for Mentoring & Transportation → 02·c Reading Tutoring Every kid deserves to learn to read. What it is Reading Tutoring is one-on-one literacy support for CCS students. Volunteers complete VA Literacy Partnerships certification before being matched, then meet weekly with the same student through the school year. What you'd do A one-hour session each week, in the school day or just after, at one of CoP's partner schools. VA Literacy Partnerships provides the training and the curriculum. Your job is to show up consistently for the same student over a school year. 40% Black students reading on grade level (CCS) 89% White peers, same grade 1 hr weekly with the same student Cert required VA Literacy Partnerships 1:1 Tutoring School-year long Sign up for Reading Tutoring → 03 How to sign up The same flow, for all three roles. Account, matching form, interview, match notification. Background check is run by CoP in parallel. 01 Create a portal account Sign up at volunteer.cityofpromise.org with your name, email, and a password. About a minute. 02 Matching form Background, interests, weekly availability, and the role(s) you would consider. You can pick one role or all three. 03 Interview A 15-to-20-minute conversation with CoP's Assistant Director, by phone or in person. Both sides decide whether to move forward. 04 Match notification When CoP pairs you with a family, student, or pod, you get an email and onboarding starts from there. 04 — Start here All four steps live in the portal. Account creation, matching form, interview scheduling, and ongoing engagement all happen at volunteer.cityofpromise.org . Same portal for current volunteers, who sign in there to log shifts and update availability. Open the Volunteer Portal → I'm already signed up → ↗ external · volunteer.cityofpromise.org

title: City of Promise — What We Do
body: What We Do Three programs. One family. A cradle-to-career continuum for kids and the adults who raise them, because education is a social issue no school can solve alone. 01 Program One Community Schools Community School Coordinators embedded at seven Charlottesville school sites : ELC, Trailblazer, Tall Oaks, Summit, CMS, Lugo-McGinness, and CHS. After-school tutoring four days a week, on-site food pantries, and the Walking Bus that gets 25–30 kids to and from Trailblazer every day. 7 CCS school sites 75% drop in absences (Spring→Fall 2025) 40+ hours added instruction 4×/wk after-school tutoring Coordinators On-Site Tutoring Food Pantries Walking Bus Resource Brokering See how it works → Meet our coordinators → 02 Program Two Dreambuilders Dreambuilders is a two-year wraparound program for working Charlottesville families: parent classes, family learning time, embedded coaching, and up to $7,000 in micro-financing to invest in self-sufficiency. 2 yr commitment per family $7K in micro-financing Weekly parent + family learning NCFL evidence-based model Parent Time P.A.C.T. Time Micro-Financing School Coordination Program Details → Who qualifies → 03 Program Three Family Engagement & Advocacy The parent-facing arm of our model offers parenting coaching, school advocacy, and connection to the wider Charlottesville safety net , because a child's trajectory tracks their parent's. Any CoP family can start a conversation, no application required. 1:1 parent coaching All CoP families eligible Ongoing intake, no cohorts LIFT integrated team model Parenting Practices School Advocacy Academic Involvement Community Support What parent support looks like → Start a conversation → Why three, why together Dual-generation, by design. We coach the child, support the parent, and connect the family to the "constellation of care" around them: housing, childcare, health, food. A single coordinator may touch all three programs for the same household in a single week. Read our approach → 01 Child Community Schools 02 Family Dreambuilders 03 Community Family Engagement Move this work forward. This is relationship work, not a transaction. It only happens when partners stay in for the long haul. Donate Now → Partner with us → NAP credits Gifts of $500 or more qualify for a 65% Virginia state tax credit. CoP has used 100% of its allocation each year, so credits move fast.

title: Who We Are — City of Promise
body: On this page Team Board History Partners Who We Are Place-based. Dual-generation. Charlottesville. Founded in 2010 in Westhaven and 10th and Page. Ten staff and twelve board members work across seven Charlottesville City Schools, out of an office at 708 Page Street. Team Our team. Price A. Thomas Executive Director Jermaine Dias Assistant Director Crystal Johnson Community School Director Melissa Steppe Director of Parent Engagement & Advocacy Tiffaney Morris Administrative Specialist Dawn Lawson Family Empowerment Coach Zeneida Howard Family Empowerment Coach Jamar Henderson Community School Coordinator Shaunquitta Wright Community School Coordinator Jamaala Hamilton Community School Coordinator Board of Directors Governance. Chair Shawn Pendleton, ChFC First Vice President of Investments, Stifel Nicolaus & Company Chair Emeritus Bill Shenkir, PhD, CPA William Stamps Farish Professor Emeritus, Former Dean, UVA McIntire School of Commerce Vice Chair Leah Puryear Director of Upward Bound, University of Virginia Lance Blakey Battalion Chief, Charlottesville Fire Department Brian Williams Associate Professor of Public Policy, UVA Frank Batten School of Leadership and Public Policy Katie Ryan Associate Professor, UVA Law School Shamia Hopkins Assistant Manager, Aramark Tracy Downs, MD, FACS Chief Diversity and Community Engagement Officer, UVA Health Brent Percival Executive Director, Jefferson Trust Phil Stinnie Dean of Student Life, Director of Community Engagement, Field School Kamela Yelder Founder, Sincere Dreams, LLC Munier Ahmad Nazeer Program Director for Mentoring & Community Engagement, UVA Women's Center History Our history. 2010 · Founded in Westhaven One of the federal Promise Neighborhoods, set up to deliver cradle-to-career support to kids and their parents in a single Charlottesville zip code. 2016 · First Pathway coaches The coaching layer that became the backbone of Community Schools. 2019 · Dreambuilders launched Dreambuilders, the two-year wraparound program for parents and their children, ran its first cohort. 2022 · Embedded in 7 school sites Community School Coordinators were placed inside Trailblazer, Tall Oaks, Summit, and four other CCS schools. 2026 · Pathways to Family Success coalition CoP convenes Charlottesville's family-support organizations under one coordinated coalition. City of Promise was founded in 2010 as a federal Promise Neighborhood, with a cradle-to-career model that worked with kids and their parents together in Westhaven and 10th and Page. Sixteen years later, the office is still on the same block, at 708 Page Street, and Community School Coordinators are now in Trailblazer, Tall Oaks, Summit, and four other Charlottesville City Schools. Dreambuilders, our two-year wraparound program for parents and their children, came online in 2019, and Family Empowerment Coaches followed not long after. Between Spring and Fall 2025, average absences among CoP students dropped 75%, and in FY26 we convened the Pathways to Family Success coalition to bring Charlottesville's family-support organizations together. Partners Partners. The schools, funders, faith partners, and community organizations whose work overlaps with ours every week, in the same buildings, with the same families. Be the tailwind. Kids spend about 80% of their waking hours out of school. We work in those hours. Donate Volunteer Partner with us
